description: Ravagers is a team of high school students from Bintulu, Sarawak whom are interested to learn more about space. The Ravagers' goal is to create an interactive website that tells the stories of NASA's discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars, exploring their purpose, history, and lasting legacy in space exploration.
summary:
Our project, “Forgotten Footprints: The Story of NASA’s Equipment on the Moon and Mars,” is an interactive website that tells the stories of NASA’s equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. We developed the website to make information about these objects easier and more interesting for people to explore. Our website is targeted among kids aged 7-12 and also teenagers, whereas even adults.

The website provides information about different pieces of equipment, including what they were used for, where they were left, and their role in NASA’s space missions. It uses simple storytelling and visuals to help users understand the history behind each object.

This is because younger generations are only educated on active missions, but not the past missions that had a significantly huge impact on space exploration.

Our project addresses the “Abandoned but not Forgotten” challenge by showing that these objects are more than just abandoned equipment. Through this website, users can discover the history of space exploration, learn about NASA's achievements, and understand that every piece of abandoned equipment has a story worth remembering.
details:
THE RAVAGERS’s PROJECT SOLUTION

Forgotten Footprints is an educational website for both kids and adults, this website is designed to educate users about the history behind abandoned equipment by attracting the interest of younger audiences. Users get to explore and learn about every discarded equipment that was used for space exploration through storytelling.

HOW DOES THIS SOLUTION WORKS?

Our website, Forgotten Footprints, takes users on an educational journey to explore NASA equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. The website is divided into two main archives: Moon Archive and Mars Archive. Through pictures, storytelling, and interactive features, users can discover the history, purposes, missions, and contributions of each piece of equipment.

Step 1 – Choose Your Experience

Users can choose between two different experiences. Both share the same true stories and facts about NASA's equipment, but offer different styles of learning.

Step 2 – Choose Your Destination

Users can choose where they want to explore, such as the Moon Archive, Mars Archive, or Further Frontiers.

Step 3 – Explore the Archives
Users can ask the Ravager AI Bot to know more about their curiousity.

Users can explore the equipment, learn about their missions, discover their purposes, and understand their contributions through pictures and storytelling.

One question: What information or activities are included in your Further Frontiers section? I want to describe it correctly in your project explanation.

Moon Archive

• Eagle – Apollo 11 Lunar Module Descent Stage: Users discover how Eagle brought the first astronauts to the Moon and learn about the descent stage that remained on the lunar surface.

• Surveyor 3: Users learn how it studied the Moon's surface and soil before being visited by Apollo 12 astronauts.

• EASEP – Apollo 11 Science Station: Users explore the scientific experiments left on the Moon to study moonquakes and measure the distance between Earth and the Moon.

• Falcon – Apollo 15 Lunar Module: Users discover how Falcon helped astronauts explore the Moon during the Apollo 15 mission.

• Apollo 15 ALSEP: Users learn how this scientific equipment collected information about the Moon's environment and internal activity.

• Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV-1): Users discover how astronauts used this vehicle to travel across the lunar surface and collect samples.

Mars Archive

• Viking Lander 1: Users learn how it became the first successful NASA lander on Mars and studied the planet's surface and atmosphere.

• Mars Pathfinder and Sojourner: Users discover how Pathfinder delivered Sojourner, NASA's first successful Mars rover, to explore the Martian surface.

• Spirit Rover (MER-A): Users learn how Spirit explored Mars and found evidence that water once existed on the planet.

• Opportunity Rover (MER-B): Users discover how Opportunity searched for signs of ancient water and made important discoveries about Mars.

• InSight Lander: Users explore how InSight studied the interior of Mars and recorded marsquakes.

• Ingenuity Mars Helicopter: Users learn how Ingenuity became the first aircraft to achieve powered, controlled flight on another planet.

Overall, our website makes space exploration easier and more interesting to understand. By combining storytelling, pictures, and interactive learning, users can discover the achievements of these abandoned machines and understand why their contributions to space exploration should never be forgotten.

THE WEBSITE BENEFITS

This website benefits children, teenagers, students, and the wider community by:

Sharing Space History – Telling the stories of NASA equipment left on the Moon and Mars.

Increasing Knowledge – Helping users learn about NASA's missions and discoveries.

Making Learning Fun – Using pictures, interactive features, and simple storytelling to make learning more interesting.

OUR GOAL

To provide an accessible interactive platform for users , specifically the younger generation to learn and get to know more about the purpose of the abandoned equipment that was sent to space. The website aims to explore the purposes behind these missions, the discoveries made through them and how these pieces of equipment contributed to the advancement of space exploration and scientific knowledge.

DATA SOURCES

NASA official websites → Through NASA’s data, we were able to access information about abandoned equipment that was used for two planet explorations: Mars and the Moon. Furthermore, NASA provided details about each equipment's history, purpose, missions, discoveries, and its contribution towards space exploration. We used this information to create the Moon and Mars’ archive on our website. In addition, NASA images and mission records helped us present the equipment through pictures and storytelling. These sources allowed us to share true and reliable information with users while helping them understand why these abandoned machines are important to space exploration.
